recipes.name: Beef Stroganoff 1
instructions: Slice meat into thin strips about 1½ inches wide and 2-3 inches long. Sprinkle lightly with tenderizer, toss and refrigerate.

Cut off mushroom stems even with the caps and slice mushrooms. Sauté ¼ of the onions in 3 Tbs. butter until almost clear, but not brown. Add ¼ of the mushrooms and sauté until just tender. Remove to a 12 quart enamel roasting pan.
Sauté remaining onions and mushrooms in same manner, i.e., in four batches. You may need to add a little butter each time.
In same skillet in which vegetables have been cooked, brown meat a little at a time with a minimum of butter, removing it to the roasting pan as it browns.
Put in 2 cans of bouillon and the flour in a blender and blend until smooth. Set aside.
Pour remaining cans of bouillon into skillet and stir and scrape to deglaze the pan. Add bouillon and flour mixture, stirring as you add to keep smooth.
Add tomato juice and Rhine wine. Pour over the meat and vegetables in roasting pan. Season to taste.
About 1½ hours before serving, place in a 375 degree oven and bring to a simmer, stirring occasionally.
Just before serving, add sour cream and a splash of Rhine wine. Serve with buttered noodles or long grain and wild rice.
recipes.notes: Can easily be halved. Great recipe for a crowd. 375°F oven, 12 quart enamel roasting pan.

recipes.name: Beef Stroganoff 2

ingredients.name: bouillon or consommé (10½ oz can), diluted to make 2 cups

instructions: Sauté mushrooms and onion in 2 tbsp. butter and remove from pan.
Remove fat and bone from steak. Cut into strips 2½" long and ¾" wide.
Melt additional 2 tbsp. butter in pan. Toss strips of meat in flour, coating thoroughly. Brown meat in butter.
Add salt and bouillon-water mixture. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until meat is tender, about 1¼ hours.
Add mushrooms, onions and sour cream; heat. Serve over noodles or rice.
recipes.notes: Uses round steak — more economical cut. Simple, classic version.

recipes.name: Beef Stroganoff 3

ingredients.name: beef tenderloin or boneless top loin steak (½ inch thick)

instructions: Cut beef across grain into about 1½ x ½ inch strips. (Beef is easier to cut if partially frozen, about 1 hour.)
Melt margarine in 10-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Cook beef in margarine, stirring occasionally, until brown.
Reserve ⅓ cup of the broth. Stir remaining broth, the ketchup, salt and garlic into skillet. Heat to boiling; reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer about 10 minutes or until beef is tender.
Stir in mushrooms and onion. Cover and simmer about 5 minutes or until onion is tender.
Shake reserved broth and the flour in tightly covered container; gradually stir into beef mixture. Heat to boiling, stirring constantly. Boil and stir 1 minute; reduce heat to low.
Stir in sour cream; cook until hot. Serve over noodles.
recipes.notes: Quickest of the three stroganoff versions. 300 cal per serving. Lighter version: decrease margarine to 1 tbsp, use nonstick skillet and reduced-fat sour cream/yogurt for 265 cal.

recipes.name: Beef and Beer Stew
instructions: In large bowl combine flour, 2½ tsp. salt, and pepper. Add chuck, tossing to coat. Set aside.
Heat ¼ cup oil in 4 quart Dutch oven or kettle. In oil, sauté onion and garlic until tender, 8 to 10 minutes. Remove from Dutch oven.
Heat remaining oil. Add chuck, brown well on all sides.
Return onion and garlic to Dutch oven, along with beer, soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, steak sauce, bay leaves, and thyme. Mix well. Bring mixture to boiling.
Reduce heat; simmer, covered 2 hours or until meat is tender.
Meanwhile, pare potatoes, cut into quarters. Add potatoes and 1 tsp. salt to 1 inch boiling water; simmer, covered 20 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
Drain potatoes well. Toss with parsley. To serve, turn stew mixture into serving dish. Surround the stew with potatoes.
recipes.notes: Dutch oven recipe. Low and slow — hearty and rich.

recipes.name: Stay-A-Bed Stew

ingredients.name: cream of tomato soup (10¾ oz can)

instructions: Mix all ingredients together in a large casserole dish and cover tightly.
Put casserole in 275 degree oven. Let cook for 5 hours, without checking.
recipes.notes: Can also be cooked in a crock pot. 275°F, 2-3 quart casserole dish, covered. True set-it-and-forget-it.

recipes.name: Jordan Marsh's Blueberry Muffins
recipes.source: Cookbook — adapted from Marion Cunningham / Bridge Creek Restaurant, Berkeley, CA (1987)
instructions: Heat the oven to 375 degrees. Grease 12 large muffin cups. Sift together the flour, salt, and baking powder.

Cream the butter and 1¼ cups sugar in a large bowl until light. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Add to the flour mixture alternately with the milk, beating just until smooth.
Crush ½ cup blueberries with a fork, and mix into the batter. Fold in the remaining whole berries.

Fill the muffin cups with batter. Sprinkle the remaining tablespoon of sugar over the tops of the muffins. Bake until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, about 30 minutes. Cool for 30 minutes before removing from the pan.
Store uncovered, or the muffins will be too moist the second day — if they last that long.
recipes.notes: The trick is crushing some of the blueberries and folding them in — distributes blueberry flavor throughout. Legendary department store recipe from Jordan Marsh in Boston.

recipes.name: Apple, Peach or Plum Cake Cockaigne

ingredients.name: milk (enough to make ½ cup with egg and vanilla)
sliced pared apples, peaches, or unpared plums

instructions: Preheat oven to 425°. If the fruit used is very juicy, reduce the liquid in the dough by at least 1 tablespoon.
Sift before measuring: 1 cup all-purpose flour. Resift with baking powder, ¼ tsp salt, and 2 tbsp sugar.
Add 1½ to 3 tablespoons butter. Work these ingredients like pastry.
Beat well in a measuring cup: 1 egg and ½ tsp vanilla. Add enough milk to make a ½-cup mixture.

Combine with the flour and butter to make a stiff dough. Pat the dough into the pan with a floured palm or spread with a spoon, then distribute evenly by pushing with the fruit sections as you place them closely in overlapping rows.
Arrange 3 to 4 cups sliced fruit in overlapping rows on the dough.
Sprinkle with a mixture of about 1 cup sugar, 2 teaspoons cinnamon, and 3 tablespoons melted butter.
Bake about 25 minutes.
recipes.notes: Joy of Cooking classic — 'Cockaigne' denotes a personal favorite of the authors. Works with apples, peaches, or plums. 9x9x2½ inch pan.

recipes.name: Swedish Meatballs
instructions: Put everything in a bowl together and mix it to an even batter (it should NOT be runny!).
Grab a pinch of the mixture and roll it until it resembles a meatball. Repeat until you've used all the mixture.
Put them in a frying pan on medium heat, fry evenly until cooked through.
recipes.notes: Grandma didn't write down spice measurements — start small, make one and taste it, adjust from there. Tip: wet your hands when rolling and they won't stick. 500g ≈ 1.1 lbs.

recipes.name: Elizabeth Frink's Roast Lemon Chicken
recipes.source: NYT Cookbook — from The Artists' and Writers' Cookbook
instructions: Heat the oven to 325 degrees. Place the chicken in a large baking dish and season inside and out with salt and pepper.

Remove the skin from 1 lemon in strips with a vegetable peeler, and rub the skin over the outside of the chicken. Quarter the lemon and squeeze the juice over and into the chicken. Put the lemon pieces and garlic cloves inside the cavity.

Melt the butter with the olive oil in a small pan. Pour about one-third of the butter mixture inside the chicken. Tie the legs together with kitchen string. Pour the remaining butter and oil over the chicken. Re-season the top.
Roast the chicken for 1½ hours, or until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the leg registers 165 degrees, basting every 15 minutes with the pan juices.
Half an hour before the chicken is done, pour the juice from the second lemon over the chicken and sprinkle with the parsley.

Transfer the chicken to a cutting board to sit for 15 minutes before carving. Pour ½ cup water or broth into the roasting pan and place it over high heat. Scrape up the pan drippings with a wooden spoon. Reduce the pan juices to the desired consistency, and season to taste.
Carve and serve the chicken, passing the sauce on the side.
recipes.notes: The technique is all about repetitions of lemon — peel on skin, juice over, pieces in cavity, second lemon 30 min before done. Great cold too — makes excellent sandwiches on brioche.

recipes.name: Roasted Broccoli with Butter and Mustard

ingredients.name: broccoli, cut into 1½ to 2-inch florets, stems sliced ¼-inch thick

instructions: Heat the oven to 450 degrees. On a baking sheet, toss the broccoli with the olive oil, salt and pepper. Arrange in a single layer, cut-sides down, and roast, without flipping, until browned and crisp-tender, 15 to 20 minutes.
Add the butter, vinegar and mustard to the broccoli on the sheet pan and toss until the butter's melted, scraping up browned bits from the pan as you go. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
recipes.notes: Dead simple side dish. The butter-vinegar-mustard combo on roasted broccoli is surprisingly good.

recipes.name: La Scala Chopped Salad

ingredients.name: grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan cheese

instructions: Add all dressing ingredients (olive oil, red wine vinegar, garlic, Dijon mustard, salt, pepper, and Pecorino Romano) to a small bowl or jar. Whisk together or seal and shake to combine.
In a large bowl, combine shredded iceberg lettuce, romaine lettuce, chickpeas, Italian salami, and mozzarella cheese.
Pour dressing over the salad and toss to coat. Serve immediately. Store leftovers in the fridge for 1-2 days; keep dressing separate if prepping in advance.
recipes.notes: A copycat of the famous La Scala Beverly Hills chopped salad. Can substitute dry mustard (1 tsp) for Dijon (3 tsp). Dress separately to prep ahead.

recipes.name: Roasted Sweet Potato Salad with Lentils

ingredients.name: sea salt and pepper to taste

instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Slice sweet potatoes into small wedges and place on baking sheet. Drizzle with 1 tbsp olive oil, toss to coat. Sprinkle with cumin, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper; toss again.
Bake sweet potatoes for 45-55 minutes total.
While sweet potatoes bake, cook lentils: bring 3 cups water to boil, add lentils, reduce to simmer, cook covered 4 minutes. Remove from heat and leave covered 2-3 more minutes. Drain.
Prep garlic: slice top off half bulb, drizzle with 1 tsp olive oil and pinch of salt. Wrap tightly in parchment or foil.

When 20 minutes remain on sweet potatoes, remove from oven. Add drained lentils and toss with sweet potatoes. Place wrapped garlic bulb in corner of baking sheet. Return to oven for 20 more minutes until garlic is aromatic and sweet potatoes are caramelized.
Make dressing: whisk together parsley, tahini, lime juice, 1 tbsp olive oil, cumin, salt, and pepper. Add 4-5 tbsp water and whisk to desired consistency.
When done baking, squeeze roasted garlic into dressing and whisk until combined.

Add sweet potatoes and lentils to a large bowl. Drizzle with half the tahini dressing and toss. Top with chopped almonds, capers, and fresh parsley. Drizzle remaining dressing on top. Serve immediately.
Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days.
recipes.notes: Can use pre-cooked or canned lentils to save time. Cashew butter can substitute for tahini for a milder, sweeter flavor. Add kale, zucchini, or Brussels sprouts to the baking sheet in the last 20 minutes for extra greens.

recipes.name: Honey Mustard Quinoa Apple Salad with Crispy Shallots
instructions: Add quinoa to a medium saucepan and cover with stock. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook until all liquid is absorbed, about 15-20 minutes. Transfer to a bowl to cool.
While quinoa cooks, fry shallots: combine sliced shallots and 1/3 cup olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook 15-20 minutes until golden and crispy, stirring often. Remove from heat.
Place a sieve over a small bowl and pour in shallots, separating oil from shallots. Transfer shallots to a paper towel-lined plate and sprinkle with salt. Let oil cool at least 5 minutes.
Make vinaigrette: whisk apple cider vinegar, honey, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper into the slightly cooled shallot oil. Taste and adjust seasoning.

In a large salad bowl, combine cooled quinoa, arugula, parsley, apple slices, pepitas, and fried shallots. Drizzle vinaigrette over top and toss to combine. Grind extra black pepper on top. Top with Parmesan and enjoy.
recipes.notes: Use a sharp, crisp apple like Honeycrisp or Granny Smith. Swap pepitas for walnuts, pecans, or almonds. To make vegan, use vegetable stock and skip or sub dairy-free Parmesan. If meal-prepping, add apple fresh just before serving to prevent browning.

recipes.name: Tuscan Chicken and Spaghetti Squash

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken, cut into bite-size pieces
sun-dried tomatoes, packed in oil, drained, julienne cut

instructions: Cook spaghetti squash: pierce squash several times with a knife, place on a microwave-safe plate, and microwave on high 8-12 minutes until tender. Let cool. (Alternative: roast at 350°F for 45-60 min cut-side down.)

Season chicken with salt, pepper, and Italian seasoning. Melt 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken and cook 5-7 minutes until golden and cooked through (165°F internal temp). Remove to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 1 tbsp butter to pan. Add shallot and garlic; cook until softened, about 2-3 minutes.
Add sun-dried tomatoes and heavy cream. Bring to a simmer.
Turn off heat. Stir in Parmesan cheese and spinach until wilted. Add chicken and any accumulated juices back to the pan.
Cut cooled squash in half lengthwise, remove seeds, and scrape out strands with a fork. Stir squash into cream sauce until evenly coated.
Garnish with fresh parsley if desired and serve immediately.
recipes.notes: Low carb and gluten free. Spaghetti squash can be cooked ahead of time and reheated. Look for julienne-cut sun-dried tomatoes at the store to save prep time. Recipe assembled from Punchfork and search snippets — original page had a fetch error.

recipes.name: Whole Roasted Cauliflower with Pistachio Pesto

ingredients.name: small yellow onions, sliced 1/4 inch thick lengthwise
cilantro and flat-leaf parsley leaves, lightly packed

instructions: Position a rack in the center of the oven and heat to 400°F.
Trim cauliflower stem flush with the head so it sits flat.

Heat a 10-inch cast-iron or heavy ovenproof skillet over medium heat. Add 1 tbsp olive oil, onions, and 1/4 tsp salt. Cook, stirring, until translucent and golden at edges, 7-10 minutes. Stir in 3/4 cup water and remove from heat.

Rub cauliflower with remaining 1 tbsp oil, then pepper and remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Clear the center of the skillet and nestle the cauliflower in it. Cover pan tightly with foil and bake until a paring knife meets no resistance when inserted, 20-30 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the pesto: reserve a bit of lemon zest for garnish. Place remaining zest in a food processor with the herbs, 1/4 cup olive oil, pistachios, garlic, salt, and pepper. Pulse until well combined.

Turn oven to 450°F (or 425°F convection). Uncover cauliflower and baste with pan juices. Cook, basting occasionally and adding 1/4 cup water if pan threatens to dry out, until nicely browned, 20-30 more minutes.
Spoon pesto over top, sprinkle with reserved lemon zest and more fresh herbs, and serve.
recipes.notes: Recipe is paywalled on NYT Cooking — assembled from multiple third-party sources. Orange cauliflower preferred but any color works. Pine nuts or almonds can substitute for pistachios. The cauliflower becomes almost custardy — serve with a spoon. Works great in a Dutch oven for the covered portion.

recipes.name: Lemon Blueberry Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Butter three 9-inch round baking pans, line bottoms with parchment, butter and lightly flour.
Sift cake flour into a bowl, add all-purpose flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt; whisk 30 seconds and set aside.
In a stand mixer with paddle attachment, whip butter, sugar, and lemon zest until pale and fluffy.
In a 2-cup measuring cup, measure milk then stir in sour cream and lemon juice; let rest 3 minutes.
Mix eggs into butter mixture one at a time, then stir in lemon extract and vanilla. Toss blueberries with 3 tbsp of the flour mixture.
Working in three batches beginning and ending with flour, add 1/3 flour alternating with 1/2 milk mixture, mixing just until combined after each addition. Gently fold in blueberries.
Divide evenly among pans and bake 24–27 minutes until toothpick comes out clean. Cool in pans 20–30 minutes then invert onto wire racks.
For frosting: beat butter until pale and fluffy in stand mixer. Add cream cheese and mix until smooth. Add vanilla, lemon extract, and powdered sugar; blend until smooth.
Frost cooled layers and decorate with blueberries and lemon slices if desired. Store in airtight container.
recipes.notes: Omit lemon extract from frosting if using for a different recipe. Rinse and drain blueberries well before using.

recipes.name: Leah's Cookies

ingredients.name: milk chocolate Hershey bar, cut into 1/2" squares

instructions: In food processor or blender, process oats briefly and set aside.
Using an electric mixer, cream butter and both sugars. Add eggs and vanilla and mix well.
Combine flour, blended oats, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. Add to butter-egg mixture, blending well.
Stir in chips, candy, and nuts.
Roll into balls and place 2 inches apart on a cookie sheet.
Bake in a pre-heated 375°F oven for 6 to 10 minutes.
recipes.notes: For Tea Room, use 3/4 cup cookie dough to make a larger cookie. Recipe can easily be cut in half. Note in margin says 2 1/2 (possibly halved quantities).

recipes.name: Blueberry Mascarpone Tart

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, cut into 1/2 inch pieces

instructions: To make the crust: preheat oven to 350°F. Combine confectioners' sugar, flour, butter, salt, and lemon zest in a food processor. Process until mixture forms a ball.

Press dough into a 4.5 x 14-inch rectangular tart pan with removable bottom, pressing into the edges. Chill in the fridge for 15 minutes then bake 10–12 minutes until very light browned. Set aside to cool.
For the mascarpone filling: in the bowl of an electric mixer with the whisk attachment, whisk heavy cream until soft peaks form. Add sugar and whisk until stiff peaks form.
Switch to the paddle attachment, add mascarpone, and beat on medium-low until fully incorporated.
Pour mixture into baked tart shell. Top with blueberries and refrigerate until ready to serve.
recipes.notes: Can also be baked in a 9-inch round tart pan.

recipes.name: Soft Breadsticks
instructions: In the mixing bowl, dissolve yeast in water. Add sugar, salt, and oil; stir until dissolved.
Add 2 cups of flour; beat until smooth. Add enough remaining flour to form a soft dough.
Mix on medium speed 6–8 minutes. Place in a greased bowl, turning once to grease top. Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1 hour.

Punch dough down and divide into 12 portions. Roll each into a 10-in x 1/2-in strip. Place 1 inch apart on a greased baking sheet sprinkled with cornmeal. Let rise uncovered until doubled, about 45–60 minutes.
Beat egg white and water; brush over breadsticks. Sprinkle with coarse salt if desired.

Place baking sheet on middle rack; place a large shallow pan filled with boiling water on the lowest rack. Bake at 400°F for 10 minutes. Brush again with egg white. Bake 5 minutes more or until golden brown.
recipes.notes: Yield: 1 dozen. The steam from the water pan gives these a nice chewy crust.

recipes.name: Whipped Chocolate Ganache Layer Cake

ingredients.name: plain devil's food cake mix (18.25 oz)

instructions: Prepare the Whipped Chocolate Ganache and chill it uncovered in the refrigerator while you prepare the cake.
Place a rack in the center of the oven and preheat to 350°F. Generously grease two 9-inch round cake pans with shortening, dust with flour, and shake out excess.

Place cake mix, milk, oil, eggs, and vanilla in a large mixing bowl. Blend on low speed 1 minute. Stop and scrape down sides. Increase to medium and beat 2 minutes more. Divide evenly between pans and smooth tops.
Bake until cakes spring back when lightly pressed, 28–32 minutes. Remove and cool on wire racks 10 minutes. Run a knife around the edges and invert; allow to cool completely, 30 minutes more.
Remove the chilled ganache from the refrigerator. Whip on high speed 2–3 minutes until it lightens in color and triples in volume.
Place one cake layer right side up on a serving platter. Spread top with frosting. Place second layer on top and frost top and sides with clean, smooth strokes.
Store in a cake saver or under a glass dome in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.
recipes.notes: This cake contains more vegetable oil than other chocolate cakes and is better with whole milk. The added fat causes the cake to bake flatter — many cooks consider this a blessing for stacking. For a domed look try the Old-Fashioned Devil's Food Cake (p. 48).

recipes.name: Basic Yeast Dough
instructions: Proof the yeast using the oil and sugar in warm water.
Mix the salt into the flour in a stand mixer bowl.
After the yeast has proofed, add the yeast mixture to the flour. Knead until a dough forms, then continue kneading for an additional 5–6 minutes until dough is elastic.
Cover and let rise for about 10 minutes.
From this point you can roll it out and use it for any recipe.
recipes.notes: Use vegetable oil instead of olive oil for sweet bread recipes. A very quick and versatile base dough.

recipes.name: Soft Dinner Rolls

ingredients.name: beaten egg mixed with a pinch of salt (glaze)

instructions: Preheat oven to 70°C (155°F) for proving. Butter a deep 9x13 inch baking pan and line with non-stick foil.
Put the milk and butter in a measuring jug. Melt in microwave for 1.5 minutes. Add sugar and salt and stir well, then add to stand mixer bowl.
Measure 175ml of very hot water into the jug and add to the mixer bowl.
Add about half the flour and mix with the dough hook for 1 minute. Add the yeast, mix a little, then add the rest of the flour.
Allow the dough to knead for 5 minutes, scraping down if necessary. Scrape soft dough into center, cover with cling film, and allow to prove for 5 minutes.
Rub a little oil onto a clean worktop and tip the dough out. Cut into quarters, then each quarter into 3 to give you 12 pieces. Roll into balls and place in the prepared pan.
Brush with beaten egg and pinch of salt. Place in the 70°C oven for 20 minutes or until buns have risen to the top of the pan.
Turn the oven to 180°C/350°F (whilst tray is still in) and bake for another 15–18 minutes until golden brown.
recipes.notes: The low oven temp trick for proving is the key to this recipe. Don't preheat — just put straight in the cool warm oven.

recipes.name: Basic Cream Scones
instructions: Sift together flour, salt, and baking powder. With a pastry cutter, cut in butter until roughly pea-sized.
In a small bowl, beat eggs until foamy. Add cream and sugar and beat well.
Combine wet ingredients with the dry and fold gently to combine. Stir as little as possible. Add currants or desired extras.
Using your hands, gather dough into a rough ball and place on a floured counter top. Pat into a disc about 3/4 inch thick. Cut into triangles with a sharp knife or use a cookie cutter.
Place in an airtight container or bag and freeze, OR bake at 450°F for 10 minutes. Serve warm.
To bake from frozen: Preheat oven to 425°F. Place frozen scones on baking tray and bake 12–16 minutes, or until slightly golden.
recipes.notes: Variations/Extras: zest of 1 lemon/orange/lime, toasted chopped nuts, 1/4 cup dried currants, chopped candied ginger, dried cranberries, sharp cheddar cheese (grated).

recipes.name: Roasted Turkey with Garlic, Rosemary and Roasted Lemon with Cremini Mushroom Gravy

ingredients.name: fresh turkey (16 pounds), rinsed and patted dry
kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Remove turkey from refrigerator 30 minutes before roasting.

Rub the cut side of 2 halves of garlic over the entire turkey and put in the cavity. Brush entire turkey with 4 tablespoons butter and sprinkle with rosemary, salt, and pepper. Put 2 lemon halves in cavity.
Put the shallots, carrots, celery, remaining garlic, and lemon halves in the bottom of a roasting rack pan. Place turkey on the rack. Add 2 cups of stock to the pan.
Put remaining 4 tablespoons butter and 4 cups stock in turkey cavity. Roast approximately 3 hours 15 minutes, basting occasionally, until internal temperature reaches 165°F.
See full recipe at source URL for complete gravy instructions.
recipes.notes: Serves 6–8. Prep 40 min, Inactive 50 min, Cook 3 hr 15 min. Full instructions including cremini mushroom gravy available at the Food Network link.

recipes.name: Great-Great Grandmother Zezulka's Goulasch

ingredients.name: beef (or half beef/half pork), cubed and fat removed

instructions: Brown onions in melted margarine until edges are browned. Add paprika and mix. Stir in meat.
Cook until meat lets out its juices. Add garlic and tomato sauce. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until most of the juice boils out.
Sprinkle flour over mixture, stirring well. Cover completely with water, stirring until thickens.
Add caraway seed and marjoram. Cook over low heat — the longer the better. Serve over egg noodles.
recipes.notes: Recipe by Eva (Riha) Hahn. The longer this cooks over low heat, the better it gets.

recipes.name: Fluffy Buttermilk Biscuits

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
cold unsalted butter, cut into small cubes
large egg, beaten with 1 tbsp water (egg wash)

instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Add cold butter to the flour mixture. Use a pastry cutter or fingers to work the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Make a well in the center and pour in the cold buttermilk. Stir until just combined — dough will be sticky.
Turn dough out onto a floured surface and knead gently a few times until it comes together. Pat into a rectangle about 1 inch thick.
Use a floured biscuit cutter to cut out biscuits. Place on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Brush tops with egg wash and sprinkle with flaky sea salt.
Bake for about 35 minutes or until golden brown. Serve warm.
recipes.notes: Pair with creamy sausage gravy, whipped honey, or alongside fried chicken.

recipes.name: Cheater Cheater Chicken and Dumplings

ingredients.name: evaporated milk in the can (1 + 1/2 can)

instructions: Strip the meat from the rotisserie chicken. Cover the meat and throw the carcass into a pot covered with chicken broth and water to cover. Season with salt, pepper, and a little poultry seasoning. Bring to a boil and simmer about 1.5 hours to build flavor.
Remove all carcass pieces and parts with a strainer or spider. Add optional fresh thyme sprigs while broth builds.

For the dumplings: liberally sprinkle work surface with flour. Arrange biscuits on the flour. Sprinkle with salt, pepper, and poultry seasoning. Roll out very thin (larger than your hand). Cut with a pizza wheel into strips.
Gather the dumpling pieces with flour and let rest on a plate. The more flour you pick up, the thicker your broth will be.

Bring broth to a boil and add dumplings. They'll puff up at first — don't worry, they'll thin back out. Add butter and evaporated milk and stir a few times. Cook on medium to medium-high boil for about 15 minutes.
Turn off heat (or low heat) and add the cooked, shredded rotisserie chicken.
Note in margin: Top with pie crust and dab of butter, heat in oven to brown crust, serve over rice.
recipes.notes: The dumplings thin out and the broth thickens — it's like magic. Add chicken back at the end to keep it from overcooking. Variation: top with pie crust + butter, brown in oven, serve over rice.

recipes.name: Red Velvet Cake
instructions: Cream sugar and oil; add eggs and beat well. Add vinegar and food coloring; beat well.
Sift dry ingredients; add alternating with buttermilk. Add vanilla; beat well. Pour into cake pan.
Bake at 350°F for 30 to 35 minutes.
For frosting: cream oleo and cream cheese; add vanilla and sifted sugar. Mix well. Add nuts; spread on cake.
recipes.notes: From Jo Ann Poerner's kitchen. A classic Southern recipe on a vintage recipe card.

recipes.name: Lemon Poppy Seed Teacake
instructions: Using an electric mixer, cream the butter in a large bowl. Gradually beat in 1¼ cups sugar. Beat in the lemon zest, orange zest, and poppy seeds. Add egg yolks one at a time, beating thoroughly after each addition. Beat until the mixture is very light.
In a separate bowl, beat the egg whites until they form soft peaks. Gradually add ¼ cup sugar and beat until whites are stiff but not dry.
Add the flour and salt, ⅓ at a time, to the egg yolk mixture, folding it in after each addition.
Stir in ¼ of the egg whites into the flour-egg yolk mixture, then fold in the remaining whites. Pour into a 10-inch bundt pan that has been greased and floured.
Bake in a pre-heated 350°F oven for about 1 hour, or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean. When done, let stand 5 minutes. Remove from pan and place on a wire rack.
In a small non-aluminum saucepan, combine lemon juice and remaining ¼ cup sugar. Heat just until sugar is dissolved. Slowly drizzle over warm cake. Serve with Peach Tree Lemon Sauce.
recipes.notes: Makes 16 servings. One of the Tea Room's first desserts — light and very tasty. Serve each slice with a dollop of lemon sauce and garnish with a mint leaf and fresh violet.

recipes.name: Chocolate Devil's Food Cupcakes

ingredients.name: instant espresso granules dissolved in 1/2 cup warm water

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line muffin tin with paper liners or spray with non-stick cooking spray.

In the bowl of a stand mixer (or with a hand mixer), beat together the cake mix, pudding mix, sour cream, oil, eggs, vanilla, and espresso water mixture. Beat for about 2 minutes on medium speed until well combined.
Using a large cookie scoop, distribute the batter between 24 muffin wells — about 3 tablespoons per well.
Bake 18–22 minutes or until tops spring back when lightly touched. Cool inside muffin tins about 10 minutes.
Remove cupcakes and allow to fully cool on a wire rack. Once cool, top with your favorite buttercream.
recipes.notes: The espresso granules enhance the chocolate flavor without making the cupcakes taste like coffee.

recipes.name: Milk and Honey Cake

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, at room temperature, plus more for greasing
honey, plus more for whipped cream and serving

instructions: Heat oven to 350°F. Grease two 8-inch round cake pans, line bottoms with parchment paper and grease the parchment.
Sift flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt into a large bowl.
In a small bowl, beat eggs until smooth.
In a medium bowl, stir together buttermilk, honey, and vanilla.
Using an electric mixer with paddle attachment, beat butter on medium speed to break it up, then gradually beat in sugar, continuing until very light and fluffy, 2–3 minutes.
With the mixer on medium, add eggs 1 tablespoon at a time. If the mixture looks curdled, add 1 tbsp of the flour mixture to bind it.

Reduce mixer to low and mix in a third of the flour mixture. Scrape down sides, then mix in half the buttermilk mixture. Mix in another third of flour, remaining buttermilk, then remaining flour. Scrape down bowl.
Scrape batter evenly into prepared pans and smooth tops. Bake until cake springs back when pressed and toothpick comes out clean, 30–40 minutes.
Transfer to wire rack to cool 10 minutes. Run offset spatula around edges, unmold onto rack, remove parchment and cool completely.

Just before serving, whip cream with a drizzle or two of honey to taste. Frost top of one cake, top with second layer, then frost the top of the stacked cake. Drizzle with additional honey and garnish with berries.
recipes.notes: Full recipe available at NYT Cooking link.

recipes.name: No-Knead Dutch Oven Bread

ingredients.name: active dry or highly active dry yeast

instructions: In a large bowl, stir together the flour, salt, and yeast. Stir in water using a wooden spoon until the mixture forms a shaggy but cohesive dough. Do not over-work. The less you work it, the softer the bread.
Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let rest at room temperature 12–18 hours (overnight is ideal).
Preheat oven (with Dutch oven inside) to 450°F for 30 minutes.
While your Dutch oven preheats, turn dough onto a well-floured surface. With floured hands, form into a ball. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let rest.
After 30 minutes, carefully remove Dutch oven. Place bread dough into it (you can put a piece of parchment under the dough if your Dutch oven isn't enamel coated).
Replace cover and bake 30 minutes covered. Carefully remove cover and bake 7–15 minutes more, uncovered, until deep golden brown.
recipes.notes: Special cookware needed: Dutch oven or any large oven-safe dish/bowl with lid. Over 286,000 shares — a very popular recipe!

recipes.name: Beef Carbonnade (Belgian Beer Beef Stew)

ingredients.name: boneless beef chuck roast (English cut preferred), cut into 1-2" pieces

instructions: Cook on LOW in slow cooker for 8 hours.

About 20–30 minutes before serving, bring a big pot of water to a boil for egg noodles. Mix 2 tbsp flour and 3–4 tbsp beef broth until no lumps remain. Stir into beef stew in slow cooker. Increase heat to HIGH and cook uncovered 10–15 minutes.
Add egg noodles to boiling water and cook according to package directions. Drain and toss with a bit of olive oil or butter and a pinch of minced parsley.
To serve, add egg noodles to a bowl or plate. Top with beef carbonnade and sprinkle with more parsley. Alternatively, add noodles to slow cooker and ladle together.
recipes.notes: Steps 1-3 (browning beef, softening onions and garlic, adding beer and broth) cut off in image — see The Chunky Chef website for complete beginning instructions.

recipes.name: Beer Beef Stew
instructions: Heat oil in large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Season beef. Working in 2 batches, brown meat on all sides, 6 minutes. Remove to plate.
Add onion to pot and reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring, until softened, 3 minutes. Add garlic and cook, stirring, 1 minute.
Pour in beer. Add broth, tomato paste, Worcestershire, sugar, paprika, 1/2 tsp kosher salt, and pepper to taste.
Return beef to pot. Simmer until meat is tender, 1.5 to 2 hours.
Stir in potatoes and carrots. Simmer until vegetables are tender and meat is very tender, 30–40 minutes more.
Remove 1 cup of liquid and slowly whisk in flour. Stir back into pot and bring to gentle boil. Reduce heat and simmer until thickened, 10 minutes. Season. Sprinkle with parsley and serve with bread.
recipes.notes: Serve with crusty bread. Distinct from Belgian Carbonnade (r033) — this uses pale lager, potatoes, and carrots for a more traditional stew.

recipes.name: Lemon Curd Tart
instructions: Pre-heat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Prepare the lemon curd by whisking the egg yolks, whole eggs, sugar, lemon juice, and lemon zest over a bain marie (a large bowl placed over a pan of simmering hot water).
Once the mixture thickens, add the butter and whisk until combined. Pour into the pre-baked tart shell and bake until set.
Chill before serving.
recipes.notes: Step 3 was partially cut off in the original image. Full instructions at Tasty.co.

recipes.name: Jalapeño Ranch (Chuy's Copycat)
instructions: Combine jalapeño, garlic, and cilantro in a blender or food processor. Pulse until finely chopped.
Add light sour cream, ranch dressing mix, and lime juice and pulse to combine.
Add milk and pulse. Add slowly to get the consistency you want — Chuy's version is pretty thin, so about 6 tablespoons.
Refrigerate for a few hours to allow the flavors to combine, though it's amazing right away too.
recipes.notes: Chuy's copycat. Thin it out more with extra milk for closer to the restaurant version.

recipes.name: Pret A Manger Porridge
instructions: Simmer oats in water for a few minutes.
Add the milk, simmer until oats are cooked through.
Top with your favourite items.
recipes.notes: Official Pret A Manger recipe. Oat milk works well as a dairy-free alternative.

recipes.name: Maple French Toast Swirl Bagels
instructions: Mix all dough ingredients together (except the cinnamon paste) and knead until smooth. Start with 400g bread flour and add more if dough feels too tacky.
Incorporate the cinnamon paste but don't over knead — this gives the marbling effect. Cover and proof the dough for 1–2 hours or until almost doubled in size.
Divide the dough into 6 equal sections and shape into balls. Cover and let rest for 15 minutes.
Shape the bagels. Make sure to seal the edges well. Place each on individual sheets of parchment paper and proof for 30 min–1 hour until noticeably puffy (they don't need to fully double).
When bagels are almost done proofing, preheat oven to 425°F and bring a large pot of water to a gentle simmer. Add a spoonful of barley malt syrup and 1 tsp baking soda.
Working in batches, boil each bagel 30 seconds each side, then transfer to a baking sheet. Sprinkle tops with cinnamon sugar mixture.
Bake for 18–22 minutes or until deeply golden brown.
recipes.notes: Plump, soft, chewy, subtly sweet with maple, cinnamon, and brown sugar flavors. The partial cinnamon paste incorporation creates the swirl marbling effect — don't over-knead after adding it.

recipes.name: Spicy Avocado Ranch
instructions: Add everything except the additional buttermilk to a jar and blend with an immersion blender. You can also throw everything into a blender.
Add additional buttermilk at the very end to get to desired consistency — usually about 1 extra tablespoon.
recipes.notes: From @chacekitchen on Instagram. Adjust jalapeño to your spice level.

recipes.name: Homemade Queso (No Velveeta)

ingredients.name: pepper jack cheese, shredded (8 oz block)

instructions: In a bowl whisk together the cream, salt, pepper, cumin, onion powder, garlic powder, and cornstarch. Set aside. Grate the cheese and measure out the sour cream.
Chop jalapeño and onion. Sauté them in the butter on low heat until tender but not browned.
Add in the cream and spices mixture. Bring to a low boil, stirring constantly to prevent sticking.
Add the sour cream, mix and bring back to a low boil or simmer. Turn off the heat and mix in the cheese.
Taste and add more salt if needed. The mixture will be thick yet somewhat thin — it will continue to thicken as it cools.
Can be served immediately. Store in the refrigerator and reheat in a skillet on low heat.
recipes.notes: For spicier queso, add two jalapeños. Mixture thickens more as it cools. Made with sour cream and pepper jack — no processed cheese needed.

recipes.name: Abir's Sourdough Bread
instructions: Mix the starter and water together before adding the rest of the ingredients.
Once all ingredients are incorporated, allow to rest for 1 hour before doing 4 rounds of stretch and folds every 30 minutes.
Allow to bulk ferment at room temperature until 25% larger or doubled in size (takes about 6+ hours).
Shape the dough and place into a basket to cold ferment in the fridge overnight (or up to 48 hours).
When ready to bake, preheat Dutch oven at 450°F. When fully preheated, take loaf out of fridge, lightly coat in flour, and do a quick scoring.
Place in the oven for 30 minutes with lid on, then 15 minutes with lid off. Let loaf rest for at least 1 hour before cutting.
recipes.notes: Recipe shared via DM by @chillhaveabir (Abir Zahra). Distilled water is specified — may help with consistency.

recipes.name: Crispy Rice Teriyaki Chicken Salad

ingredients.name: Persian cucumbers (or 1 large English), thinly sliced

instructions: Prepare the crispy rice: preheat oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment. Add cooled rice and toss with sesame oil and teriyaki sauce, spread into an even layer. Bake 30–35 minutes, tossing halfway through.
Remove bones from rotisserie chicken, shred into small pieces, and toss with teriyaki sauce. Set aside.
Make the dressing: add all dressing ingredients to a blender and blend about 1 minute until smooth.
Chop/slice all salad ingredients and add to a large bowl.
Add shredded chicken and crispy rice on top. Pour dressing over the salad, toss, and enjoy. Store in refrigerator up to 5 days.
recipes.notes: Handwritten notes on recipe: substitute green cabbage and carrots for some items. Also add +2 tbsp Ponzu to dressing and use Tahini instead of cashew butter. Double the ginger and add 1/2 lemon.

recipes.name: Jordan Marsh's Blueberry Muffins
recipes.source: NYT Cooking / The New York Times (cookbook)
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F. Grease 12 large muffin cups. Sift together the flour, salt, and baking powder.
Cream the butter and 1¼ cups sugar in a large bowl until light. Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Add to flour mixture alternately with the milk, beating just until smooth.
Crush ½ cup blueberries with a fork and mix into the batter. Fold in the remaining whole berries.
Fill muffin cups with batter. Sprinkle the remaining 1 tablespoon of sugar over the tops of the muffins.
Bake until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, about 30 minutes. Cool 30 minutes before removing from the pan.
Store uncovered, or the muffins will be too moist the second day.
recipes.notes: The legendary muffins from Jordan Marsh department store in Boston. Mashing some of the blueberries before adding to the batter is the key technique. Makes 12 large muffins.

recipes.name: Coconut-Miso Salmon Curry

ingredients.name: medium red onion, halved and sliced 1/2 inch thick
fresh ginger (1-inch piece), peeled and minced
salmon fillet (1.5 lb), cut into 2-inch pieces
fresh lime juice, plus lime wedges for serving
hot steamed jasmine or basmati rice, for serving

instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, ginger, and garlic; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 3 minutes. Add the miso and cook, stirring frequently, until miso is lightly caramelized, about 2 minutes.

Add the coconut milk and 3 cups water; increase heat to high and bring to a boil. Cook until liquid is slightly reduced, about 5 minutes. Stir in the salmon, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer gently until just cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Turn off the heat and stir in the spinach and lime juice.
Divide the rice among bowls. Top with the salmon curry, basil, and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing on top.
recipes.notes: Light, delicate weeknight curry — comes together in less than 30 minutes. Flaky white fish, shrimp, or scallops work well too. For heat, garnish with sliced jalapeño or serrano chile.

recipes.name: Ang's Creamy Tortellini Soup

ingredients.name: half and half or heavy cream
Parmesan and fresh parsley for serving

instructions: In a large stockpot over medium-high heat, cook the sausage, breaking up into little pieces. Once browned, add onion, celery, and carrot; sauté for 5 minutes or until vegetables are softened.
Add the garlic, spices, and tomato paste; sauté for an additional 3–5 minutes, stirring to prevent burning.
Add wine and let it cook out for a few minutes. Stir the flour into the sausage and vegetables until dry. Gradually add chicken broth, stir to combine. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the cream, then bring to a low simmer. Add the tortellini and spinach. Cook tortellini according to package directions. Serve with fresh parsley and Parmesan.
recipes.notes: Total time 40 minutes. Serves 6–8. Named 'Brooke's Creamy Tortellini Soup' on the original saved PDF.

recipes.name: Brown Butter Cheesecake

ingredients.name: cookie crumbs (graham, digestive, or golden Oreos with cream removed)
browned butter (use mostly the flavorful brown bits)
cream cheese (2 blocks, 8 oz each), softened
browned butter (filling, use the reserved brown bits)
vanilla bean (scraped) or 2 tsp vanilla paste/extract

instructions: Brown the Butter: In a medium saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Continue cooking until butter foams, sputters, then goes quiet. Watch for brown bits to form at the bottom and a nutty aroma to develop. Pour into a heatproof bowl, scraping all the brown bits, and let cool.

Make the Crust: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Mix cookie crumbs, ground pecans, powdered sugar, and ½ cup plus 1 tablespoon of the browned butter (the yellow part) until evenly combined. Press into the bottom and halfway up the sides of a greased and parchment-lined 8 or 9-inch round cake pan. Bake for 10 minutes. Remove and let cool. Reduce oven to 325°F (163°C).

Prepare the Filling: In a large bowl, beat the softened cream cheese with brown sugar, salt, vanilla, and reserved brown butter bits until smooth. Add sour cream and mix until fully incorporated. Finally, add eggs and mix just until blended — avoid overmixing to prevent cracks.

Bake the Cheesecake: Pour filling into the cooled crust. Place the cake pan into a larger roasting pan and fill the outer pan halfway with hot water (water bath). Bake 60–75 minutes until the center jiggles slightly and edges are set. Turn off the oven, crack the door open, and let cool inside for 30 minutes. Remove and cool on the counter for another 30 minutes, then chill for at least 8 hours.
Whip the Topping: Combine heavy cream, brown sugar, vanilla, and a pinch of salt. Beat until soft peaks form. Spread over chilled cheesecake before serving.
recipes.notes: The reserved brown bits from the butter go into the filling for maximum nutty flavor. The water bath prevents cracking. Chill at least 8 hours — overnight is best.

recipes.name: Tuscan White Bean Kale Salad

ingredients.name: canned white beans, drained and rinsed
jar sun dried tomatoes (7 oz), drained and chopped

instructions: Make the dressing: In a food processor or blender, add the parsley, garlic, walnuts, and lemon zest. Pulse until finely chopped. Add lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Blend on high until combined to desired consistency — leave some choppiness to the herbs and nuts. Add up to 2 tbsp water to thin.
Place the kale in a bowl with a squeeze of lemon juice. Massage until no longer firm.
Add in the remaining salad ingredients and fold in the dressing until combined.
recipes.notes: Borderline addictive and extremely nourishing. The sun-dried tomatoes add a delicious depth of flavor and the gremolata dressing is lovely. Great as a main salad or side.

recipes.name: Butter Bean Zucchini Skillet

ingredients.name: canned butter beans (2 x 400mL cans), drained

instructions: Thinly slice the zucchini and onion, peel and mince garlic, and cut the peel off half the lemon and slice into thin strips.
Toss zucchini in 1 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt and pepper. Air fry at 425°F for 15–18 minutes, flipping a couple times, or oven-roast at 400°F for 20 minutes, flipping halfway.
To a non-stick pan on medium-low heat, add remaining olive oil and sliced onions, stirring often. After a few minutes, add the minced garlic and lemon strips, continuing to stir often.
Drain and rinse the butter beans, setting aside 2/3 cup for the sauce.

Turn down onions to low. To a blender, add about 1/3 of the sautéed onions and lemon from the pan, 2/3 cup of butter beans, tofu, nutritional yeast, salt, juice of the entire lemon, and water. Blend until smooth and creamy.
Add remaining butter beans to the pan, then add sauce from blender and bring to a simmer.
Remove from heat, dish up, top with the roasted zucchini and chopped fresh basil. Serve with toasted sourdough bread.
recipes.notes: The dish that will convert bean haters. The blended butter bean + tofu sauce creates a rich, creamy texture without dairy. Great with toasted sourdough.

recipes.name: Elise's Pumpkin Bread
instructions: In a large bowl: combine flour, pumpkin pie spice, baking soda, and salt.
In a medium-size bowl: combine sugar, pumpkin, eggs, oil, and orange juice. Beat until just blended.
Add pumpkin mixture to dry mixture. Stir until just moist.
Spoon batter into 5 greased/floured small 5x3 disposable loaf pans OR 2 regular-sized loaf pans.
Bake at 350°F for 50–55 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean. Cool in pan 10 minutes.
recipes.notes: Recipe noted on handwritten card as also having an extra 2 tsp pumpkin pie spice (written as '+ 2 tsp pie spice'). Makes 5 small or 2 regular loaves.

recipes.name: White Linen Cocktail
instructions: Muddle cucumber slices in a shaker.
Add gin, elderflower liqueur, simple syrup, and lemon juice. Shake with ice.
Strain into a glass over fresh ice. Top with soda water.
Garnish with a cucumber ribbon. Optional: salt spray on top.
recipes.notes: From @likeablecocktails. Can swap gin for vodka or tequila. A light, refreshing cocktail — a crushable summer drink.

recipes.name: Classic Beef Stroganoff

ingredients.name: bouillon or consommé, diluted to make 2 cups

instructions: Sauté mushrooms and onion in 2 tbsp butter and remove from pan. Remove fat and bone from steak. Cut into strips 2½" long and ¾" wide.
Melt additional 2 tbsp butter in pan. Toss strips of meat in flour, coating thoroughly. Brown meat in butter. Add salt and bouillon-water mixture.
Simmer, stirring occasionally, until meat is tender, about 1¼ hours. Add mushrooms, onions, and sour cream; heat.
Serve over noodles or rice.
recipes.notes: 6 servings. From a classic vintage cookbook. Simple and hearty.

recipes.name: Chicken-Fried Steak with Gravy
instructions: Cut 1 lb round steak in 4 pieces. Dip in seasoned flour, then in egg and 2 tbsp water beaten together. Dip again in flour.
Brown on both sides in hot fat. Cover and cook slowly 20 to 30 minutes.
To make gravy: remove meat. Add ¼ cup seasoned flour mixed with 2 cups milk. Stir until gravy comes to a boil; boil 1 minute.
Return steak to gravy and serve.
recipes.notes: 4 servings. From same vintage cookbook as the Classic Beef Stroganoff.

recipes.name: Matt's Favorite Chocolate Chip Cookie
recipes.source: King Ranch Kitchen (Tina Munoz family recipe)

ingredients.name: butter (1 stick), softened to room temp

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease a cookie sheet with butter or nonstick spray.
In a large bowl, combine flour, baking soda, and salt; set aside.
In a stand mixer fitted with paddle attachment, cream butter and both sugars together until fluffy.
Beat in the eggs, one at a time, then the vanilla.
Gradually add the dry ingredients in 4 batches, mixing in between until thoroughly blended.
Stir in chocolate chips and walnuts, just until incorporated.
Drop well-rounded teaspoonfuls onto the greased cookie sheet, spaced 3 inches apart.
Bake for 8–10 minutes, until set and golden at edges. Cool on wire rack.
recipes.notes: IMPORTANT: Over-baking makes crisp cookies (handwritten note on recipe). Tina Munoz's family recipe, shared through the King Ranch Kitchen for 4 generations.

recipes.name: King Ranch Casserole
recipes.source: Family cookbook (Mrs. Frank Birkhead (Janet) and Mrs. Bob Batte (Gerry))

ingredients.name: cream of mushroom soup (10¾ oz can)
cream of chicken soup (10¾ oz can)
Ro-Tel tomatoes and green chilies (10 oz can)

instructions: Cook chicken in small amount of water, lightly salted, until tender. Bone and cut into pieces.
To make a sauce, blend until smooth the two cans of soup, can of tomatoes and green chilies, and chicken broth.
Into a greased 2½ quart casserole, place a layer of chicken, ½ of the tortillas cut into pieces, ½ of the onion, ½ of the cheese, and ½ of the sauce. Repeat the layers, ending with grated cheese.
Bake uncovered at 350°F for 1 hour.
recipes.notes: Great way to use leftover Thanksgiving or Christmas turkey. For a party, a 12-15 lb turkey works for 25-30 people — increase other ingredients accordingly and repeat layers 3-4 times in a large roasting pan, baking approximately 2 hours. Do not rinse canned chiles — much of the taste will go down the drain.
